In  [[probability theory]], '''Kramkov's optional decomposition theorem''' (or just ''optional decomposition theorem'') is a mathematical theorem on the decomposition of a positive [[supermartingale]] <math>V</math> with respect to a family of [[Risk-neutral measure|equivalent martingale measure]]s into the form
:<math>V_t=V_0+(H\cdot X)_t-C_t,\quad t\geq 0,</math>
where <math>C</math> is an [[adapted process|adapted]] (or [[optional process|optional]]) process.

The theorem is of particular interest for [[financial mathematics]], where the interpretation is: <math>V</math> is the wealth process of a [[Trader (finance)|trader]], <math>(H\cdot X)</math> is the gain/loss and <math>C</math> the consumption process.

The theorem was proven in 1994 by Russian mathematician [[Dmitry Kramkov]].<ref>{{cite journal|first=Dimitri O.|last=Kramkov|title=Optional decomposition of supermartingales and hedging contingent claims in incomplete security markets|journal=Probability Theory and Related Fields|volume=105|pages=459–479|date=1996|doi=10.1007/BF01191909|doi-access=free}}</ref> The theorem is named after the [[Doob-Meyer decomposition]] but unlike there, the process <math>C</math> is no longer [[predictable process|predictable]] but only adapted (which, under the condition of the statement, is the same as dealing with an [[optional process]]).

== Kramkov's optional decomposition theorem ==
Let <math>(\Omega,\mathcal{A},\{\mathcal{F}_t\},P)</math> be a filtered probability space with the filtration satisfying the [[usual conditions]].

A <math>d</math>-dimensional process <math>X=(X^1,\dots,X^d)</math> is ''locally bounded'' if there exist a sequence of [[stopping time]]s <math>(\tau_n)_{n\geq 1}</math> such that <math>\tau_n\to \infty</math> [[almost surely]] if <math>n\to \infty</math> and <math>|X_t^i|\leq n</math> for <math>1\leq i\leq d</math> and <math>t \leq \tau_n</math>.

=== Statement ===
Let <math>X=(X^1,\dots,X^d)</math> be <math>d</math>-dimensional [[càdlàg]] (or RCLL) process that is locally bounded. Let <math>M(X)\neq \emptyset</math> be the space of [[equivalent local martingale measure]]s for <math>X</math> and [[without loss of generality]] let us assume <math>P\in M(X)</math>.

Let <math>V</math> be a positive stochastic process then <math>V</math> is a <math>Q</math>-[[supermartingale]] for each <math>Q\in M(X)</math> if and only if there exist an <math>X</math>-integrable and predictable process <math>H</math> and an adapted increasing process <math>C</math> such that
:<math>V_t=V_0 + (H\cdot X)_t-C_t,\quad t\geq 0.</math><ref>{{cite journal|first=Dimitri O.|last=Kramkov|title=Optional decomposition of supermartingales and hedging contingent claims in incomplete security markets|journal=Probability Theory and Related Fields|volume=105|page=461|date=1996|doi=10.1007/BF01191909|doi-access=free}}</ref><ref>{{cite book|title=The Mathematics of Arbitrage|first1=Freddy|last1=Delbaen|first2=Walter|last2=Schachermayer|date=2006|publisher=Springer Berlin|place=Heidelberg|page=31}}</ref>

==== Commentary ====
The statement is still true under change of measure to an equivalent measure.
